handbookNote: Tennessee Real Estate Broker license exam. Genuinely NEW track -- Tennessee previously had no broker-tier track on this site, only tn_re_salesperson (Affiliate Broker / salesperson-equivalent). Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the Tennessee Real Estate Commission (TREC). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly reading PSI's own official Tennessee Real Estate Candidate Information Bulletin (copyright 2025, updated 7/1/2025, fetched from PSI's own candidate-bulletin hosting -- WebFetch's own summarizer failed to extract readable text from the PDF on first attempt, so the raw saved PDF was read directly via the Read tool, per this project's standard workaround). Exam Summary Table, quoted directly from the bulletin: Broker exam = 125 total scored items across two separately-scored portions -- a National portion of 75 items (80 points possible; a small number of items are worth up to 2 points each, disclosed here rather than silently treated as 1 point apiece) with a 150-minute time limit and 75% passing (60 of 80 points), and a Tennessee State portion of 50 items with a 90-minute time limit and 75% passing (38 of 50 items); combined total time 240 minutes (4 hours). A small number of unscored pretest items (the bulletin says 5-10) may also appear and are already folded into the 125. This site's track_registry schema models one combined question-count/duration/pass-percent per track rather than two separately-scored portions, so the DB row records the combined totals (125 questions, 14400s/4hr duration, 75% pass, min_correct=94 as the nearest whole-item rounding of 125 x 0.75) -- the two-portion, two-timer, separately-scored real structure is disclosed here and in the track's description/mechanicsNote copy so users aren't misled into thinking it's a single undifferentiated 125-item sitting. CONTENT OUTLINE, quoted verbatim from the bulletin's own content-outline percentages (National portion, Broker column, summing to exactly 100% of the 75-item national portion, independently re-verified by hand this session): Property Ownership 10%, Land Use Controls 5%, Valuation 8%, Financing 9%, Contracts 19% (the largest single national topic), Agency 13%, Property Disclosures 7%, Property Management 5% (Broker-specific sub-items on manager supervisory duties and property-management trust handling), Transfer of Title 6%, Practice of Real Estate 12% (Broker-specific sub-items on timeshare/commercial-industrial/property-management specialty practice areas), Real Estate Calculations 6%. Tennessee State portion, quoted verbatim as item counts (of the 50-item state portion, Broker column): Duties and Powers of the Real Estate Commission 6 items; Licensing Requirements 5 items; Advertising and Marketing 7 items; Broker and Affiliate Relationships 6 items; Handling of Documents and Record Keeping 6 items; Handling of Trust and Escrow Funds 7 items; Other Improper Activities and Consumer Protection 3 items; Agency and Disclosure Issues 7 items; Special Areas of Practice 3 items -- summing to the full 50-item state portion. This bank's bucket sizing is directly proportional to these real, PSI-published weights (each national bucket's target count scaled off its published % of the 75-item national portion; each Tennessee bucket's target count scaled off its published item-count out of the 50-item state portion), not an even split -- actual per-bucket counts were then set by each drafting pass to whatever its real, verifiable source material actually supported (several buckets landed a few questions above or below their proportional target for exactly this reason; nothing was padded to hit a round number). Real Tennessee statute/rule facts independently verified this session (via findlaw.com full-text extracts -- Justia and the TN Secretary of State's own rules site returned 403s on direct fetch during this build, so findlaw and law.cornell.edu served as the working primary-text mirrors) and used as pinpoint citations: T.C.A. Title 62, Chapter 13 (Tennessee Real Estate Broker License Act of 1973) in its entirety, with specific sections including Sec. 62-13-102 (definitions, incl. affiliate broker), Sec. 62-13-104 (licensing exemptions, incl. owner-of-property and limited resident-manager exemptions), Sec. 62-13-112 (errors and omissions insurance requirement, exemption for acquisition agents, license-suspension consequence of a lapse), Sec. 62-13-201 through 208 (Commission composition/authority, incl. Sec. 62-13-208's real estate education and recovery account -- confirmed via live full-text pull to be the correct Recovery Fund citation, correcting an initial research guess of Sec. 62-13-501, which is actually in the unrelated Part 5 'Commercial Real Estate Brokers' subchapter), Sec. 62-13-301 through 320 (licensing/renewal/CE/reciprocity/branch-office requirements, incl. Sec. 62-13-310(b)'s sign-lettering advertising rule and Sec. 62-13-320's broker-to-affiliate-broker voluntary status conversion), Sec. 62-13-312(b) (the full enumerated disciplinary-grounds list, pulled and cited by specific paragraph number -- misrepresentation, undisclosed compensation, failure to disclose a licensee's own interest in purchasing a listed property, 3-year record retention, dual representation without written consent, failure to supervise affiliate brokers, and the Commission's discretionary remedy of downgrading a broker's license to affiliate-broker status as an alternative or additional disciplinary tool), Sec. 62-13-321 (trust/escrow account 3-year record retention specifics -- depositor, deposit date, withdrawal date, payee), and Sec. 62-13-401 through 407 (Part 4, Representation by Real Estate Agents -- agency creation, limited agency status, statutory duties to all parties and to clients, written disclosure timing/content requirements, designated agency, facilitator status) confirmed via live findlaw full-text pull. Also cited: the Tennessee Time-Share Act of 1981 (T.C.A. Title 66, Chapter 32, Part 1 -- acquisition-agent licensing, 30-hour training, dual-license restriction); the Tennessee Human Rights Act housing provisions (T.C.A. Sec. 4-21-601, cross-referenced to Sec. 62-13-312(b)(13) as independent license-discipline grounds); and federal law cited for genuinely national financing/disclosure content -- RESPA Section 8 (12 CFR 1024.14/.15), TILA/Regulation Z (12 CFR 1026.19/.23), the TRID 3-business-day Loan Estimate/Closing Disclosure timing rules, ECOA/Regulation B (12 CFR 1002), and the federal pre-1978 lead-based-paint disclosure rule. TREC Rule Chapter 1260-02 (the Commission's own procedural rules, distinct from the Title 62 statute) is cited by specific subsection only where independently confirmed live this session -- Rule 1260-02-.09 (trust/escrow/trustee account requirements: separate account, no commingling, timely deposit, the 21-day earnest-money interpleader process, disbursement bases, interest-account recordkeeping) and Rule 1260-02-.12 (advertising: firm-name and principal-broker-approval requirements, blind-ad prohibition, franchise/co-op and team-name disclosure, sign-consent rules, website/IDX/VOW disclaimers, the one-click social-media disclosure rule); a small number of rule-level facts that could not be pinned to a confirmed subsection (e.g. the exact listing-agreement termination-date rule location, and the affiliate-broker firm-transfer administrative process) are deliberately hedged to the general statute/rule chapter rather than assigned a guessed subsection number, per this project's grounding standard -- flagged in-bank via each such question's own source_note rather than silently presented as pinpoint-confirmed. Standard national real-estate/appraisal/finance/contract-law/math content not tied to a Tennessee-specific statute (property ownership, land-use-control theory, valuation approaches and calculations, agency doctrine, real-estate math formulas, deed types, title/closing mechanics) is sourced to 'national real estate contract law principles' / 'PSI national content outline' framing throughout, consistent with this project's standard for generic/national content never presented as a pinpoint state citation. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate Broker track rate (nj_re_broker.json, ny_re_broker.json, ga_re_broker.json, pa_re_broker.json, ca_re_broker.json, fl_re_broker.json, oh_re_broker.json, tx_re_broker.json, mi_re_broker.json). This bank was drafted across six parallel content-authoring passes grouped by real content-outline topic clusters (three national/national-adjacent buckets per pass on average), each pass instructed to draft every question with the correct answer as choice_a, then deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_tn_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 20 bucket files combined, in file order -- final distribution 25.1/25.0/25.0/25.0%). One genuine cross-bucket near-duplicate was found and removed by manual review before rotation (two different buckets independently drafted a near-identical 'alternative disciplinary remedy: downgrade broker to affiliate-broker status' question under different fact patterns and different topic labels -- caught by comparing shared source_note citations across all 20 files, since the automated per-topic dedup in build-track-batch.js cannot catch a duplicate that spans two different topic strings; the copy in 19_broker_affiliate_relationships.json was kept as the more natural conceptual home, the copy in 20_handling_of_trust_escrow_funds.json was deleted). All remaining draft questions passed an automated schema/weight-range/distinct-choice validation pass, and were additionally run through this project's standard Jaccard-similarity dedup check (scripts/build-track-batch.js) at build time to remove any further exact or near-duplicate items before loading. POST-BUILD CORRECTION (2026-09-02): discovered this build's six drafting passes had been given a per-bucket target computed from a fixed item-count-times-multiplier formula, and 4 of the resulting buckets (Property Management, Land Use Controls, Real Estate Calculations, Transfer of Title) landed suspiciously exactly on that target -- clear anchoring, not a genuine content ceiling. Standing policy corrected project-wide: pool ratios are a floor to check after drafting, never a target given to a drafting agent. Ran a full backfill: de-rotated all 20 files back to the choice_a-correct convention, relaunched the 4 flagged topics with no ceiling (added 17/20/14/17 respectively), re-checked cross-bucket dedup (1 new near-duplicate found -- Advertising and Marketing vs. Broker and Affiliate Relationships, both citing T.C.A. 62-13-312(b)(18)'s self-dealing disclosure fact almost verbatim; kept in Broker and Affiliate Relationships, the more natural conceptual home, deleted from Advertising), re-rotated the full set, and rebuilt. FINAL: 632 questions (up from 565) -- a 5.06:1 pool ratio, fully reloaded into D1 (565 old rows deleted, 632 new rows inserted, verified by count).
